newsitem.title: PERU: Peru mother asks Japan PM to find rebel's corpse.
newsitem.headline: Peru mother asks Japan PM to find rebel's corpse.

text.p: The mother of a Tupac Amaru rebel killed in Peru's hostage rescue raid at Tokyo's diplomatic residence called on Saturday for Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to help find her daughter's corpse.

Eligia Rodriguez wrote to Hashimoto, who was in Lima for one day to thank Peru for resolving the four-month hostage crisis, and asked him to "use his good influence with the Peruvian government so that they give me the body of my daughter."

The military killed all 14 of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) hostage-takers in an explosive assault on April 22. But the guerrillas' bodies were hurriedly buried by authorities in cemeteries scattered throughout Lima and in many cases relatives were not allowed to see the bodies.

The whereabouts of only two rebel corpses are known. The bullet-ridden bodies of MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa and his second-in-command Rolly Rojas are buried in humble graves in mass cementeries under the constant vigil of intelligence service agents.

Leading Peruvian human rights group, Aprodeh, which published Rodriguez' letter to Hashimoto, has called for the bodies of the two rebel girls killed in the raid to be exhumed so that they can be properly identified.
"They have buried my daughter in an anonymous grave but I do not even know in which cementery," Rodriguez wrote.

Hashimoto termed Peru's end to the crisis "admirable" but human rights groups have called for an investigation into reports that troops executed at least two rebels and gunned down others who were trying to surrender.
